title: Advanced Sentence Correction — Multiple Errors
tagline: Year 3 — Finding and fixing two errors at once: agreement, tense, parallelism, modifiers, prepositions and comparatives

introduction.overview: In advanced sentence correction a sentence contains more than one error, and the right answer must fix all of them. Wrong options usually fix one error and leave another, or fix one and add a new one. The method is to scan the sentence for the common error families (agreement, tense, parallelism, modifiers, comparatives, prepositions), list the errors, and then choose the option that clears the list.
introduction.placementRelevance: Sentence-correction items with more than one error are used in verbal sections of company tests to separate strong candidates.
introduction.realWorldContext: Proofreading emails and reports for several errors at a time is the same skill.

learningObjectives: Scan a sentence for all error families
Fix subject-verb agreement and tense together
Use elimination by checking each option for leftover errors

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Singular subjects take singular verbs; tenses must agree within the sentence; items in a list must have the same form.

coreDefinitions: Subject-verb agreement: the verb matches the subject in number.
Tense consistency: past events use past tenses in sequence.
Parallelism: items in a list have the same grammatical form.
Dangling modifier: a modifier whose subject is not the sentence subject.
Idiomatic preposition: the preposition that always goes with a word (good at, fond of).
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Treat the sentence as a checklist of possible errors. Each wrong option misses one item on the checklist.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Scan for the verb and its subject, then tenses, then the list items, then prepositions. Write each error in the margin. Reject any option that leaves one of them.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Conditionals
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: If + past perfect, would have + past participle
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: If I had known, I would have come

mainNarrative: Take: "The team of engineers are working on the project, and it have almost finished." The subject is "team" (singular), so "is working". The pronoun "it" takes "has". Fixing only the first leaves "it have"; fixing only the second leaves "team… are".
Look for list items. "She like swimming, to cycle and going for long walks" has an agreement error (likes) and a parallelism error (swimming, cycling, going). Both must be fixed.
Tense sequence: "By the time we reached the station, the train already left" needs "had already left" because the leaving happened before reaching. "We have to wait" becomes "we had to wait".
Conditionals: "If I would have known… I will have attended" is wrong in both halves. The correct pattern is "If I had known… I would have attended".
Check each option for leftovers. An option that fixes the first error but introduces or keeps another is a trap.

deepDiveAspects.title: Collective nouns
deepDiveAspects.content: A team, committee or family takes a singular verb when acting as one unit.

deepDiveAspects.title: Comparatives
deepDiveAspects.content: Use -er for two things (the taller of two) and -est for three or more.

solvedExamples.title: Two verbs
solvedExamples.question: "The team of engineers are working on the project, and it have almost finished." What are the two errors?

steps.title: Error 1
steps.explanation: "Team" is singular, so "are working" should be "is working".

solvedExamples.title: Parallel list
solvedExamples.question: "She like swimming, to cycle and going for long walks." What are the errors?

steps.title: Error 2
steps.explanation: The list should be swimming, cycling and going.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Items in a list need the same form.

solvedExamples.title: Tense sequence
solvedExamples.question: "By the time we reached the station, the train already left." What is the error?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Earlier event uses the past perfect.

steps.title: Order
steps.explanation: The train left before we reached.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The earlier past needs the past perfect.

shortcutMethods.title: Error checklist

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Read it and pick what sounds right.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Scan for agreement, tense, parallelism, modifier and preposition errors; list them; choose the option that clears the whole list.

rulesForApplication: Two errors, one option fixes both.

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Count errors before looking at options.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Drop options that keep an error you have already spotted.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The correct option usually looks plain and unremarkable.
